newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russians kill six at Tajik-Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Russians kill six at Tajik-Afghan border.

text.p: Russian border guards shot dead six people who tried to cross the Tajik-Afghan border in two separate incidents, a spokesman for the border guards said on Sunday.

In one shooting late on Saturday, Russian border forces stationed in Tajikistan killed four people of unknown nationality trying to cross the border from Afghanistan and detained two others, the spokesman said from the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

Officials found 74 kg ( 160 lbs) of opium among the belongings of the dead. In another incident nearby, Russian border guards came under fire from the Tajik side about 15 minutes later. Two attackers were killed and one Russian border guard was lightly injured, the official said.
In Dushanbe, unknown asailants used grenade launchers and
machine guns on Saturday to attack a base near the airport where Russia keeps helicopters and other military supplies for its peacekeeping troops.
No one was injured and there was no damage, the border guard spokesman said.
There have been several similiar attacks on that base in recent months.

The three attacks occurred just hours after Tajikistan's government and Islamic opposition signed a military agreement on Saturday, marking a major step towards a peace settlement in the Central Asian state.

The accord, signed in Moscow in the presence of Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and the U.N. special envoy on Tajikistan, Gerd Merrem, sets out a four-step plan to integrate the armed opposition into the army.
Russia keeps a large military presence in the remote mountainous republic of 5.7 million people, both as border guards and as internal peacekeepers.
A ceasefire has largely held in Tajikistan since the December accord, but Western observers say the two sides' inability to control rogue bands roaming the mountains may jeopardise peace efforts.
